_summary: A/B test of an execution upgrade in the step that turns the planner's high-level plans into actual legal robot moves (the 'realizer').

Plans often ask a helper robot to park on a cell so the moving robot can slide into it and stop; the old realizer always parked the helper first, then ran the moving robot's whole slide sequence in one go.
Some plans only work the other way around: the moving robot walks up close first, then the helper parks, then one final slide stops against the helper.

The new opt-in mode (strict_moves(..., two_phase=True)) tries the old order first and, only when that fails at a helper-assisted step, re-runs that step in the walk-up-first order (approach, park helper, final slide); no other reordering and no extra fix-up moves are ever added.

Tested against the stored 450-problem benchmark: the 239 problems the old realizer already executed and the 211 where it failed (failed plans loaded from analysis/artifacts/failing_plans.pkl; working plans regenerated on CPU, bit-identical to the stored run, using the planner code exactly as it was when the benchmark was recorded).
All 239 previously-working problems return exactly the same move count as before: 0 regressions.
Of the 211 previous failures, 44 now execute fully into legal move sequences (each verified move by move against the game physics).
Those 44 solutions average 8.91 moves, 1.59 moves more than the shortest possible solution for those problems ('regret' = extra moves versus the known optimum, d_star).
If switched on, the benchmark solve count would rise from 239 to 283 of 450 (53% -> 63%); the mode is OFF by default and no existing caller changed.

An earlier analysis estimated ~52 fixable failures at regret ~1.90, but that prototype also reordered whole plan steps freely; 9 of its fixes need freedoms this deliberately-minimal change excludes (it also fixes 1 plan the prototype missed).
provenance_notes: Failing plans: analysis/artifacts/failing_plans.pkl (dict bench450 row index -> PartialPlan, 211 entries, written by diag_pass2.py).

Passing plans: regenerated with the diag_failures.py recipe (CPU, torch.manual_seed(0), k=5, 1200 expansions, AStar(max_iters=4000, max_frontier=40000), no realize-check, full 450-instance loop in bench450 order) and with skeleton/ shadowed at its git-HEAD state: the working tree carries an uncommitted self-support fix in skeleton/astar.py made AFTER the stored run, which changes regenerated plans (10/60 diverged in a probe without the shadow, 0 with it). All 239 regenerated passing plans matched the stored abstract cost and stored strict move count exactly.
Newly-fixed realizations were additionally replayed move by move with simulate.slide on the full joint state (44/44 legal, totals match, target reached).
Old-vs-new default path: the pre-edit strict_moves was run next to the refactored one on all 211 failing plans with captured logs -- identical returns and identical log lines (211/211).
